text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Returning from Italy, Oil Minister Dan Etete says Italian state electricity company Enel has now agreed to lift Nigerian liquefied natural gas, reversing an earlier decision to cancel a long-term contract to buy the gas.
- National Electoral Commission NECON is ready for local council elections scheduled for March 15, says its spokesman.
- Stockbroking firms to each pay 50,000 naira for use of new clearing facilities to be launched by the stock exchange next week.
- Former senator David Dafinone and member of the Vision 2010 committee shaping Nigeria's future advocates that Nigeria should quit OPEC to maximise gains from its crude oil.
- Aspirants for next month's local government elections will on Friday know whether or not they have been cleared by screening committee to be candidates in the poll.
- Former Nigerian head of state retired General Yakubu Gowon visits South Africa; meets Vice-President Thabo Mbeki and also holds discussions with Durban Oil Refinery management.

- Nigerian International Merchant Bank successfully raises its capital base to 506 million naira in line with new regulations requiring banks to shore up their capital base to a minimum of 500 million naira from 50 million naira previously.
- Prices of cooking gas fall as seven-year-old butanisation project to pipe gas into Nigerian homes nears completion.
- Demand for forex at weekly auction rises to $95.4 million from $86.262 million last week, showing higher demand over the last one month than budgeted by the authorities for the auction.
- Chevron Corp's Escravos gas project in midwestern Nigeria to be commissioned on May 1, company sources say.
- Nigeria records $30 million trade surplus with Brazil, thanks to crude oil export to the South American country, says Brazilian ambassador to Nigeria, Geraldo Muzzu.
